quote: Somebody somebody's been using my name to get stuff, in the past.
stewart_read: First disclosure of identity fraud; rep treats it as an administrative footnote ('Alright. That's good.') rather than a trust gift requiring acknowledgment.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep could be trying to stay on script to avoid derailing into a long conversation — but the schema explicitly treats vulnerability disclosure as higher priority than procedure.
coaching_implication: Pause and acknowledge specifically before returning to the qualifier: 'I'm sorry to hear that — that's a lot to deal with' before circling back to credit.

quote: has been, run through, a bunch of fraudulent activities.
stewart_read: Second disclosure touch; rep pivots straight to a Credit Karma suggestion, treating a fraud victim's concern as a logistics question.
coaching_implication: This is the second unaddressed touch of the same disclosure — rep should have flagged internally that this needed a human response, not a tool recommendation.

quote: I'm 81 years old. These assholes are about 20, 30, 40 years old
stewart_read: Third and most severe disclosure touch — elder fraud victim describing hospitalization and property loss — met with 'They did.' and a return to script.
coaching_implication: This is the moment a manager should replay directly with the rep: a real human crisis disclosure got a two-word response before closing the call.

quote: You say you have a design already?
stewart_read: Customer's confusion suggests the intro didn't clearly land what the call is for; rep clarifies but the interest question is never asked at all per verified events, so there's no emotional anchor for the rest of the call.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be normal early-call confusion from an elderly customer rather than an intro failure.
coaching_implication: Skipping interest_in_solar removes the anchor the rep could have used later when things got difficult — nothing to tie the appointment value to.

quote: Okay. So has the roof not been replaced since?
stewart_read: Rep mishears/miscommunicates the roof-age question, forcing the customer to repeat himself and clarify shingles vs. roof twice.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive fumbling rather than strategic — no evidence of a deliberate reason to confuse this question.
coaching_implication: Slow down and ask one clear question ('How old are the shingles?') instead of ambiguous phrasing that requires customer correction.

quote: And so just reach back out to us when it is. Okay? Have a great rest of your day. Bye bye.
stewart_read: Call ends with no owned next step from the rep — the customer is told to call back, no callback time is set, no button-up occurs.
coaching_implication: Even on a stalled qualifier, rep should own the follow-up ('I'll call you back Thursday to check on that') rather than leaving it entirely on the customer.
